Both of those seem to be primarily targetting JavaScript. Since all of the JavaScript code we now have is automatically generated, there is imo not much point in that right now.

I already enabled `cargo format` and `clippy` for the rust part of the codebase, let's add more (JS / Python) formatters once we write more of those languages, I guess.
Don't you always assign this in `from`? It kinda looks like the whole `RefCell<Option<..>>` is redundant. Or is it there so that you can borrow it mutably in `stream_body`?
Can node.js/python bindings handle panics in rust code? I.e., convert them to exceptions?

Yes, the `RefCell` is for the mutable borrows in functions without mutable `self`. `napi` enforces stricter rules on mutability and borrows because of (I'm assuming) sharing the data between different environments. 

E.g. asynchronous functions with `mut& self` are [edit] considered unsafe [/edit], async functions with Env argument ([docs](https://napi.rs/docs/concepts/inject-env)) are banned altogether (won't compile), for usage see e.g. the `json` function on response.

bytes are `Option<>` bcs sometimes, we haven't read the response yet. `inner` is `Option<>` so we can consume it with the `bytes` or `bytes_stream` call and we don't end up with a `RefCell` with undefined value.


There could absolutely be a better solution to all this. If you see one, I'm all ears!

Nope, I think it cannot handle those (you'd have to return `Result<_, napi::Error>` in order to do that). 

Good point - a user calling `.body` twice probably doesn't deserve to have their script killed on spot. I'll revise those calls and likely add some tests for this.
The response body is now stored in a JS `Response` instance, this solution has been dropped completely. Resolving this convo for now.
I revised the calls, hopefully, the codebase is now more beginner-user-friendly. There are still `panic` macro calls, but only in the most unexpected (and irreparable) states. Resolving for now.

`ImpitBody::from_stream(stream.into_bytes())`

would read better like:
`ImpitBody::from_bytes(stream.into_bytes())`
or 
`ImpitBody::from_stream(stream)`
or 
`...`

(Not talking implementation here, but method name and argument do not match)
